Question:
Tori’s mathematics test had \(75\) problems: \(10\) arithmetic, \(30\) algebra, and \(35\) geometry problems. Although she answered \(70\%\) of the arithmetic, \(40\%\) of the algebra, and \(60\%\) of the geometry problems correctly, she did not pass the test because she got less than \(60\%\) of the problems right.

How many more problems would she have needed to answer correctly to earn a \(60\%\) passing grade?
Solution:
The sections have different numbers of problems, so first find how many answers she got right in each section. Her correct counts are
\[
\begin{aligned}
0.70\cdot10&=7&&\text{arithmetic},\\
0.40\cdot30&=12&&\text{algebra},\\
0.60\cdot35&=21&&\text{geometry}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Thus she answered \(7+12+21=40\) problems correctly.

A passing grade requires \(60\%\) of all \(75\) problems:
\[
0.60\cdot75=45.
\]
She therefore needed \(45-40=5\) more correct answers to reach exactly \(60\%\), choice \(\text{B}\).
